LESSON: READING 14.2.1 SUMMARISING: ARGUMENTATIVE TEXTS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.2: Reading 14.2.1 Summarising: Argumentative texts

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 14.2.1 Summarising: Argumentative texts. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we write summaries?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. pick out the main points discussed in a text
2. organise an outline of points into a coherent whole
3. summarise a text correctly in their own words

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. pick out the main points discussed in a text
   In simple words: practise until you can pick out the main points discussed in a text. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. organise an outline of points into a coherent whole
   In simple words: practise until you can organise an outline of points into a coherent whole. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

3. summarise a text correctly in their own words
   In simple words: practise until you can summarise a text correctly in their own words. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 14.2.1 Summarising: Argumentative texts using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 14.2.1 Summarising: Argumentative texts in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 14.2.1 Summarising: Argumentative texts to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 14.2.1 Summarising: Argumentative texts.
4. Show that you can: pick out the main points discussed in a text

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 14.2.1 Summarising: Argumentative texts using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 14.2.1 Summarising: Argumentative texts important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read argumentative texts based on the world cup from a book or using a digital device,
2. Jointly, search the internet for more examples of reading passages and practice summarising them,
3. Digital literacy: It is promoted as the learner uses digital devices to search for reading material online.
4. Communication and collaboration: It is promoted as the learner improves their writing skills by writing summaries.
5. Critical thinking and problem solving: It is enhanced as the learner interacts with material for good summary writing skills Values:

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we write summaries?
2. Why should we learn good summary writing skills?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. pick out the main points discussed in a text
2. organise an outline of points into a coherent whole
3. summarise a text correctly in their own words

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
